title: Who Pays for Product Returns? Advertising and Return Policies
abstract: arXiv:2611.22370v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: An online marketplace decides how consumers, firms, and the platform share the cost of product returns. We study this decision when the platform earns commissions and sells prominent placement. Consumers inspect, try, and return products; firms bid for the first position and then set prices. Earlier display attracts more trials but can retain a smaller fraction of them. For small positive losses, assigning return costs to consumers raises the value of prominence relative to reimbursing firms by the same amount. Advertising therefore shifts the platform's preferred division of a given return bill toward consumers. We characterize the joint allocation for small positive return losses and give a cost condition under which the platform pays nothing. In markets with frequent returns, the platform can instead share the bill with consumers: a higher commission makes it pay more to encourage shopping and retained sales. Results at finite losses

translated_title: 谁为产品退货买单？广告与退货政策
translated_abstract: 在线市场平台需要决定消费者、企业和平台之间如何分担产品退货的成本。本文研究了当平台赚取佣金并出售显著展示位置时的这一决策。消费者检查、试用并退回产品；企业竞拍首位展示位置，然后设定价格。更早的展示位置能吸引更多试用，但可能保留更小比例的销售。对于较小的正退货损失，将退货成本分配给消费者，相比向企业报销同等金额，能提高显著展示位置的价值。因此，广告收入使平台在分摊给定退货账单时更倾向于让消费者承担更大份额。本文刻画了小正退货损失下的联合分配方案，并给出了平台无需承担任何成本的成本条件。在退货频繁的市场中，平台反而可以与消费者分担账单：更高的佣金促使平台支付更多，以鼓励购物和保留销售。
tldr: 该论文研究了在线平台如何在消费者、企业和自身之间分配产品退货成本，发现广告收入会促使平台更倾向于让消费者承担退货费用，并刻画了不同退货频率下平台的最优成本分担策略。
en_tdlr: This paper studies how online marketplaces allocate product return costs among consumers, firms, and the platform, showing that advertising revenue shifts the platform's preferred cost burden toward consumers, and characterizes optimal cost-sharing arrangements under different return frequencies.
